post.headline: How Boomers ended up with half of America's wealth
post.caption: Boomers own almost half of all wealth in America, while Millennials own almost half of all debt. It started with 76 million babies, a country built around them, and a Congress that aged right along with them. Now $84 trillion is being passed down through 2045.
post.cta: Full story and interactive charts at the link in bio.

headline.text: Boomers own half of America's wealth.

say: Almost half of all wealth in America is owned by Boomers,
while half of all debt is owned by Millennials.
Boomers have spent the last half-century molding America in their image.

scenes.query: Children of the United States in the 1950s
say: Between 1946 and 1964, about seventy-six million babies were born in America.
California was building one school a week in the fifties.
1976 was the first year Boomers could run for Congress, and they took over D.C.

scenes.source: Generation Distribution of Congress · American Inequality
say: By 2013 they held sixty percent of Congress while making up only a quarter of the population.

scenes.title: The rules they wrote
scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality
say: Those lawmakers placed limits on new housing, created tax rules that favored wealth, and protected retirement.

overlays.label: of all U.S. real estate wealth is owned by Boomers

say: Today Boomers own forty-one percent of all real estate wealth, often in large homes with few people living in them.

scenes.title: New homes with 4+ bedrooms
scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality
say: Nearly half of new homes now have four bedrooms or more, compared to one in five in the 1970s.

scenes.title: Share of all U.S. debt
say: Millennials, meanwhile, own forty-one percent of all debt, almost double the Boomers.

stats.label: held by the top 10% of Boomers

scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality
say: Now eighty-four trillion dollars is being transferred through 2045, and the top ten percent of Boomers hold most of it.
This is an opportunity to build an America with more housing, affordable education, and higher wages.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
